channel.title: Crisp & Counter — buying guides
channel.description: Five kitchen tools, five buying guides, and the source links behind every claim.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: Two appliances share a name and almost nothing else. Here is the list of differences that actually change how a weeknight goes — and the ones that only look like they do.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air-fryer capacity
item.description: The quart figure on the box answers a question you did not ask. This is the version of the question you did ask.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: The appliance that gets used is the one that is easy to put away and easy to wash. Both of those are checkable before you buy.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: Multi-function usually means one thing done well and several things done acceptably. The trick is finding out which is which before it takes up a shelf.

item.title: Is a countertop oven worth it for holiday sides?
item.description: Work backward from serving time, the pans you already own, and what actually needs the main oven.

item.title: One basket or two for Sunday meal prep?
item.description: Sketch one batch of the lunch you actually pack before buying a bigger air fryer.

item.title: Will that air fryer fit a small kitchen?
item.description: Measure the space the appliance uses in motion, not just where it sits.

item.title: Instant-read or wireless: which thermometer do you need?
item.description: Pick for the way you cook: a quick spot check at the end or monitoring during a longer cook.

item.title: Instant-read or leave-in probe: which thermometer do you actually need?
item.description: Both products in this register take a temperature. Only one of them is meant to be left alone while it does it, and that difference decides which is worth your money.
